clue.text: Four voices in combination that's noisy

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are combined and mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A vocal quartet singing together makes quite a racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in combination' signals an anagram of FOUR plus VOICES, ten letters in all; 'that's' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Vociferous describes someone loud and clamorous, shouting their views.

clue.text: Lowland farewell

explanation.surface: A goodbye said in low-lying country.
explanation.definitionFit: A vale is a valley, low ground; vale is also Latin for goodbye, used as a formal leave-taking.

clue.text: Church and state divided by unusual hatred

indicators.note: the state's letters are split apart with the other piece placed between them

parts.note: CAL is an abbreviation for California, a US state

indicators.note: unusual means the letters of hatred are put in an odd new order

explanation.surface: Church and state are split by an extraordinary animosity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' turns HATRED into ATHEDR, which 'divided by' places inside CAL; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral is the principal church of a diocese, seat of a bishop.

clue.text: Navy prison

explanation.surface: Sailors of the navy locked up in jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleet is a nation's navy or a body of warships; the Fleet was a notorious old London debtors' prison.

clue.text: One in court, trapped by factual account

indicators.note: trapped by means the other letters are enclosed within the word for factual

parts.note: factual means real

indicators.note: in places the numeral within the court abbreviation

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone in a courtroom is caught out by a truthful testimony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I inside CT to give CIT, and 'trapped by' sets CIT inside REAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a detailed narration or telling of facts, an account of events.

clue.text: Said to have issued currency

explanation.surface: Someone is reported to have put money into circulation.
explanation.definitionFit: Uttered means spoke; in law, to utter is to pass off coins or notes, especially forged ones.

clue.text: Composed a piece of classical music

indicators.note: piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A classical work that was written by a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composed' looks like a verb about writing music, but it is the definition meaning serene.
explanation.definitionFit: Composed means serene and unruffled, keeping one's cool.

clue.text: Shock for a Scandinavian climber

indicators.note: in a down clue a climber goes upwards, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a Lapp is a person from Lapland in the far north of Scandinavia

explanation.surface: A northerner scaling a peak gets a fright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climber' turns LAPP upwards to PPAL in this down clue; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is to horrify or dismay someone greatly.

clue.text: She needs a hand to get to work

definitions.text: She needs a hand to get to work

parts.words: She needs a hand to get to work
parts.note: reads like someone short-staffed wanting help, but this worker's job literally needs a client's hand to tend nails

explanation.surface: A woman needs some assistance before she can start her job.
explanation.definitionFit: A beautician who trims and polishes fingernails works on people's hands.

clue.text: When half-cut, Alfred gets unusual score in the open

indicators.note: half-cut means only the first half of the name Alfred is kept
unusual means the letters of score are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drunk Alfred racks up an odd score outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' (slang for tipsy) keeps ALF, and 'unusual' rearranges SCORE as RESCO; 'When' and 'gets' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Al fresco means outdoors, from Italian for 'in the fresh air'.

clue.text: It's used for turning a French article to an English one

parts.note: la is the French feminine definite article
the is the English definite article

explanation.surface: Switching a definite article from French to English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' hints at changing one article into another, but it is the definition: a machine for shaping by turning; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathe spins wood or metal so it can be shaped, the craft called turning.

clue.text: Stock-holder

parts.note: reads as a shareholder, but livestock are stock and this enclosure holds them

explanation.surface: An investor who owns shares.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclosure for cows keeps farm livestock penned in.

clue.text: He's willing to let others succeed

definitions.text: He's willing to let others succeed

parts.words: He's willing to let others succeed
parts.note: sounds like a generous rival, but willing means making a will and succeed means inheriting

explanation.surface: A generous man happy to see others get ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who makes a will leaves property to heirs, who succeed to it.

clue.text: Memorial of old priest outwardly Roman Catholic

indicators.note: outwardly means the letters for Roman Catholic sit on the outside, around the priest

parts.note: Eli is the Old Testament priest who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: A monument to an elderly cleric of the Catholic Church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outwardly' wraps RC around ELI; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is a keepsake or surviving object kept in remembrance of the past.

clue.text: Rocket-launcher

parts.note: reads as a missile weapon, but Rocket was a famous early steam locomotive and this is the engineer who launched it

explanation.surface: A weapon that fires missiles.
explanation.walkthrough: George Stephenson built the Rocket locomotive in 1829 for the Rainhill Trials in England.
explanation.definitionFit: The engineer George Stephenson designed and introduced the pioneering Rocket steam engine.

clue.text: Upper class marine has to work outside in storm

indicators.note: outside means the word for work goes around the other letters

parts.note: to toil is to work hard
U is the standard shorthand for upper class
RM stands for Royal Marine

explanation.surface: A posh marine labours outdoors in bad weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts TOIL around U and RM; 'has' and 'in' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A storm can mean an uproar or violent commotion, a state of chaos.

clue.text: Acting furtively, although honestly in trouble

indicators.note: in trouble means the letters of honestly are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone sneaking around despite being truthful in a jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' rearranges HONESTLY; 'although' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on the quiet means secretly, stealthily.

clue.text: Some French marry but don't expect to be happy

parts.note: des is the French word for some
to pair is to join or marry

explanation.surface: A French couple marries without expecting joy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but' is a link between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To despair is to lose all hope of a good outcome.

clue.text: A change for the better?

parts.note: reads as general improvement, but the term is a formal revision, as to a law or constitution, meant to improve it

explanation.surface: Asking whether a change has improved things.
explanation.definitionFit: An amendment is a revision made to a text or law, supposedly correcting it.

clue.text: Holder of the colours

parts.note: reads as a soldier carrying regimental flags, but colours are paints on an artist's board

explanation.surface: A soldier bearing the regimental flag.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's board holds paints for mixing.

clue.text: Point behind the ship towards the sunrise

parts.note: E is a compass point, east
astern means behind a vessel

explanation.surface: Something lies behind the boat as it heads into the dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: The sun rises in the east, so this direction faces dawn.

clue.text: They go on tiny feet

parts.note: sounds like small creatures scurrying, but these are knitted things worn on babies' feet

explanation.surface: Little creatures trotting along on small feet.
explanation.definitionFit: These are soft knitted shoes for babies.

clue.text: Poise sought by an accountant?

explanation.surface: Composure is what a bookkeeper is after.
explanation.definitionFit: Balance means steadiness or equilibrium; an accountant seeks a balance where the books tally.

clue.text: Elicit approval in a girl

indicators.note: in places the approval inside the girl's name

parts.note: Eve is a girl's name
OK signals approval

explanation.surface: Drawing a nod of agreement out of a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke is to call forth a feeling or response.

clue.text: A full round or a small portion?

parts.note: taken as written
a bit is a small portion

explanation.surface: Asking whether one gets a full helping or just a morsel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like a serving of drinks or food, but it is the definition: a complete circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbit is a complete circuit around a planet or star.

clue.text: Having risen from poverty I left Masefield floundering

indicators.note: floundering means the remaining letters struggle into a new order
left means the I has departed from the poet's name

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A speaker who rose from humble roots abandons the poet Masefield in confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' removes I from MASEFIELD, leaving MASEFELD, which 'floundering' rearranges. John Masefield was an English Poet Laureate.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-made describes someone who achieved success by their own efforts from humble beginnings.

clue.text: Drawing the French Canadian emblem

parts.note: a map is a drawing of an area
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A sketch of the national symbol of French Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French Canadian' reads as one phrase, but it splits: 'the French' gives LE and 'Canadian emblem' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Canada's flag bears a red leaf from this tree.

clue.text: Principal boy embraces heroine at last

indicators.note: embraces means the boy's letters are wrapped around the other letter

parts.note: lad means boy

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of heroine

explanation.surface: In pantomime, the principal boy hugs the heroine at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Principal boy' is the pantomime hero role, played by a woman in British pantomime, but 'Principal' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The lead is the chief or principal role or person.

clue.text: Junior officer gets warship to change direction

parts.note: a sub, submarine, is a warship
to alter is to change
N is north, a compass direction

explanation.surface: A young officer gets his vessel to turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A subaltern is a British army officer below the rank of captain.

clue.text: You can't do better than master this composition

definitions.text: You can't do better than master this composition

parts.words: You can't do better than master this composition
parts.note: put the word master before this work and you get the finest achievement possible

explanation.surface: Learning this piece of music is the best thing you can do.
explanation.definitionFit: A composition is a work, such as a piece of music or art.

clue.text: Record that makes money

explanation.surface: A document that turns a profit.
explanation.definitionFit: To note is to record or write down; a banknote is paper money.

clue.text: Though concerned, possibly resented it

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be arranged differently

explanation.surface: Though involved, someone may have felt bitter about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges RESENTED and IT; 'Though' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being concerned in something means having a stake or involvement in it.
